request: Last Seat: a seat reservation service with expiring holds. A user can hold a seat for a limited time, then confirm it, cancel it or let it expire. One seat is never sold twice, and every hold is eventually released.

Through the HTTP API a booker holds a free seat and sees that seat reported as held for them, with a deadline, for as long as the deadline has not been reached, while the other seats of the seating area are unchanged.

Start the service with the inventory ['s11','s12','s13'], a hold duration of 120 seconds and a clock the test controls, on an ephemeral port. Read GET /seats before any command and read the current time T from the demonstration clock operation. Send POST /seats/s12/holds with the body {"booker":"A"}. Then send GET /seats/s12, then advance the clock by 119 seconds and send GET /seats/s12 again, and then send GET /seats. Finally send POST /demo/clock/advance once with zero seconds and once with a number of seconds that is not whole, and send POST /seats/s11/holds with a body that names no booker.

The GET /seats taken before any command answers 200 and lists exactly s11, s12 and s13, each with status free, with no holder and no deadline. The demonstration clock answers 200 with the body {"now": <whole seconds>} and no other field. The hold answers 201 with a hold reference in UUID form and a deadline equal to T plus 120, where the test adds the duration it configured to the time it read, and does not take the service's word for it. The first GET /seats/s12 answers 200 with status held, holder 'A' and the same deadline, and with no hold reference field anywhere in the body. The advance of 119 seconds moves the reported time by exactly 119 seconds, and the seat is still reported held for 'A' with the same deadline. GET /seats lists exactly s11, s12 and s13, with s11 and s13 still free. The advance of zero seconds, the advance of a number that is not whole, and the hold that names no booker each answer 400 with reason code invalid-request and the path of the field that failed, and none of them moves the reported time or changes any seat.

The oracle fails if the seating area read before any command is missing a configured seat or reports one as anything but free, if the demonstration clock answer carries any field besides now, if an advance does not move the reported time by exactly the seconds it was given, if the deadline differs from the independently computed sum, if the held report does not name the booker, if any response body carries the hold reference after the hold itself, if s11 or s13 changes, if the seat stops being reported held before its deadline is reached, or if an advance of zero seconds, an advance of a number that is not whole or a hold that names no booker is accepted.

Through the HTTP API a second booker is refused a seat that is held or sold, a confirmation carrying a reference that was never granted is refused, every refusal leaves the whole seating area exactly as it was, and the seat ends up sold to one booker only.

Start the service with the inventory ['s11','s12','s13'] and a hold duration of 120 seconds. Hold s12 for 'A' and keep the reference. Read GET /seats. Send POST /seats/s12/holds with {"booker":"B"}. Send POST /seats/s12/holds/{a freshly generated UUID that was never granted}/confirm. Read GET /seats again. Confirm s12 with A's own reference. Read GET /seats. Send POST /seats/s12/holds with {"booker":"B"} once more and POST /seats/s12/holds/{A's reference}/confirm once more. Read GET /seats a final time.

B's first hold answers 409 with reason code seat-held. The confirmation with the never-granted reference answers 404 with reason code no-such-hold. The GET /seats taken after those two refusals is byte-for-byte the GET /seats taken before them. A's confirmation answers 200 and the seat is then sold to 'A'. B's second hold and the repeated confirmation both answer 409 with reason code seat-sold, and the final GET /seats is byte-for-byte the one taken straight after the sale.

Through the HTTP API a hold ends in every way it can: the holder cancels and the seat is free at once, nobody acts and the seat is free the moment the deadline is reached, a confirmation sent at that same moment is refused because the hold expired, the freed seat can be held by anybody, and a sold seat stays sold however far the clock moves.

Start the service with the inventory ['s11','s12','s13'] and a hold duration of 120 seconds. Hold s12 for 'A', then send POST /seats/s12/holds/{holdRef}/cancel after advancing the clock by 10 seconds, and read GET /seats/s12. Hold s12 for 'A' again, advance the clock by exactly 120 seconds so that the clock equals the deadline, read GET /seats/s12 and send POST /seats/s12/holds/{the second holdRef}/confirm. Then hold s12 for 'B' and read GET /seats/s12. Separately hold s11 for 'A', confirm it, advance the clock by 3600 seconds and read GET /seats/s11.

The cancellation answers 200 and s12 is reported free well before its deadline. change.description: Release every unconfirmed hold by cancellation or by deadline expiry

facts.text: Deliver a seat reservation service for one seating area in which a booker holds a named seat for a fixed time through a tiny HTTP API, then confirms it, cancels it or lets it expire, so that one seat is never sold twice and every hold is released.
Every operation and every observation of the service goes through the HTTP API. There is no command line interface and no other public port.
One fixed hold duration applies to every seat. It is set when the service starts and defaults to 120 seconds. A hold cannot be extended or renewed.
The deadline is authoritative. A confirm or a cancel that arrives at or after the deadline is refused with the reason 'hold expired', and the seat is reported free. There is no grace window.
Holding a seat returns a hold reference. Only the sender of that reference may confirm or cancel that hold. There are no accounts and no organizer override.
The HTTP API offers one clearly marked demo-only operation that advances the clock, so that expiry is observable during a 90-minute demonstration.
One event with one seating area is loaded when the service starts. The seat inventory cannot be changed while the service runs.
A single process holds all state in memory. Nothing survives a restart.
Every HTTP response body is structured JSON that a browser client can consume directly. No response is prose text.
Payment, accounts, waitlists, seat maps, a graphical user interface, several events, notifications, durable storage, hold extension and organizer override are out of scope.

TypeScript in strict mode, immutable data, pure functions, no 'any' and no unchecked type assertion, schema validation at the trust boundary, kebab-case file names, options objects for multi-parameter functions, and no explanatory comments in code.
After a hold is released the seat goes to whoever asks first, including the previous holder. There is no queue and no fairness promise about who gets a released seat.

Expiry is realized lazily: the stored seat record keeps a hold until a command replaces it, and one projection function compares the hold deadline with the injected clock on every read and on every command, so a hold whose deadline has passed is free at every observation. No background sweep and no timer writes to the store.

An eager sweep needs a second writer whose run can lag behind the clock, which admits a confirm after the deadline. The Quint mutant that decides on the stored record instead of the projection violates the deadline property, so any command path that reads an unprojected record breaks the authoritative deadline.

One request handler at a time owns the seat store. The Node.js runtime runs the handler body to completion without interleaving, so a hold, a confirm and a cancel each read and write the store in one uninterrupted turn.

The public seat report names the holder and the deadline but never the hold reference. The hold reference is returned once, in the response to the hold that created it. This resolves the brief's ambiguous phrase 'holder reference' and is what makes 'only the holder may confirm' observable.

The design is functional: a pure total transition over immutable seat values in the domain, with the clock, the store, the hold reference generator and HTTP kept in a thin shell. The repository holds no production code, so there is no incumbent style to preserve, and the recorded user standards require immutable data and pure functions.

Quint with the Apalache backend covers the state-transition safety claims, because they are reachability properties of a small state machine. TLA+ with TLC covers the liveness claim, because weak fairness of the clock step cannot be expressed as a Quint invariant and Apalache temporal support is experimental. Agda covers totality and the local properties of the pure transition, because those are statements about all inputs rather than about a bounded run.

The HTTP surface is: GET /seats, GET /seats/{seatId}, POST /seats/{seatId}/holds, POST /seats/{seatId}/holds/{holdRef}/confirm, POST /seats/{seatId}/holds/{holdRef}/cancel, and the demo-only POST /demo/clock/advance. A granted hold answers 201, a successful confirm or cancel answers 200, a refusal answers 409, an unknown seat or hold reference answers 404, and a body that fails validation answers 400.
The HTTP shell uses the Node.js built-in http module. No web framework is added, because the six routes above need none and every added dependency is a cost the requirement does not carry.

Zod parses every incoming request body and every path parameter at the HTTP boundary, and the response types are derived from the same schemas. The domain receives already-parsed values and never re-validates them.
Open: no business motivation was supplied for this feature and the human confirmed that none exists. The benefit behind the outcomes stays unstated. Owner: the human.

Open: a thin Svelte client on top of this API is out of scope for this feature. Whether it becomes a later value, a follow-up feature or work outside nWave delivery is undecided. Owner: the human. The design keeps every response as structured JSON so that such a client stays possible.
A restart loses every hold and every sale. The service starts again from the fixed inventory with every seat free. This is accepted, not mitigated.
The clock is assumed to move forward only. The demo advance operation accepts a positive number of seconds and refuses zero or a negative number, so the demonstration cannot move the clock backwards.

The Quint simulation run is labelled as simulation. Only the Apalache run is a bounded exhaustive check, and it is bounded: it explores runs of at most twelve steps over one seat, two bookers, a hold duration of two time units and a clock horizon of six.

The models establish properties of the design, not of a running service. They say nothing about elapsed wall-clock time, about the HTTP layer, about several processes, or about a restart. A tick in the TLA+ slice is an abstract step, never a second.

Modules under src/domain import nothing from src/app and nothing from src/adapter. The dependency direction points inward, so the pure transition stays testable and the Agda proof keeps a matching runtime subject.

The demonstration-only nature of the clock operation is carried by its route path alone: it is reachable only under the /demo prefix. Its answer body is the current time alone, as {"now": <whole seconds>}, and carries no field that marks the response as demonstration-only.

The manifest, the lock file, the TypeScript configuration and the test runner configuration are test substrate, not product. The acceptance designer writes them before the first oracle runs, because every verification recipe begins by installing the declared dependencies and no oracle can execute without a runner. Craft changes none of them.
The pure seat values and the pure transition are the single owner of every seat rule. They hold the data the rules decide on.
The application layer wires the clock, the store and the hold reference generator to the pure transition and is the single caller that persists a new seat record.
The HTTP shell, the wire schemas, the in-memory store and the clock are the edge. They translate between the outside world and the pure core and hold no seat rule.
The composition root loads the fixed inventory and the hold duration, builds the adapters and starts the server. It is the only place that chooses concrete adapters.
The repository holds no file at this path. This change creates it, so every consumer of it is created by this same change.

des code-fact answered an empty atom set over the repository root and an empty caller set for the seat operations, through the textsearch provider at noisy confidence, because the ast provider reported the target out of scope for a repository with no source file. The repository holds only documents, a licence and configuration, so no existing symbol can own any of these responsibilities.
The Node.js built-in http module already owns HTTP request parsing and response writing. It is reused rather than wrapped in a framework.
Zod already owns schema parsing at a trust boundary and is the library the recorded user standards name. It is reused for the wire schemas rather than hand-written validation.
fast-check already owns generation, shrinking and replay for TypeScript properties. It is reused for every broad law rather than a hand-rolled generator.
Vitest already owns test discovery and execution for TypeScript. It is reused as the native runner.
The driving port is the HTTP API served by the Node.js http server on a configured port. Every acceptance observation is made through it.

The Clock port answers the current time in whole seconds. One adapter implements it: an advanceable clock seeded once from the system clock when the service starts, holding an offset that the demo advance operation increases.
The SeatStore port reads the record of one seat and writes a replacement record. The only adapter keeps a frozen map in process memory.
The HoldReferences port issues one fresh opaque hold reference. The adapter uses the runtime's random UUID generator.
The Configuration port answers the fixed seat inventory and the hold duration in seconds, both read once at start.

Dependencies point inward. src/adapter depends on src/app, src/app depends on src/domain, and src/domain depends on nothing in this repository. The ports are declared in src/app/ports.ts and implemented in src/adapter.
A confirm or a cancel arrives at or after the deadline of the hold it names.
HTTP 409 with reason code 'hold-expired', and the seat is reported free by the next observation.
A hold is requested for a seat that is already held for somebody else.
HTTP 409 with reason code 'seat-held', and the seat is still reported held for its current holder with its unchanged deadline.
A hold or a confirm is requested for a seat that is already sold.
HTTP 409 with reason code 'seat-sold', and the seat is still reported sold to its owner.
A confirm or a cancel carries a hold reference that is not the reference of the hold on that seat.
HTTP 404 with reason code 'no-such-hold', so a wrong reference cannot be told from an absent one and no reference can be guessed from the answer. No observation of the inventory changes.
A request names a seat identifier that is not in the fixed inventory.
HTTP 404 with reason code 'no-such-seat' and the identifier that was sent.
A request body or a path parameter does not satisfy its schema: a missing booker name, a hold reference that is not a UUID, or an advance that is not a positive whole number of seconds.
HTTP 400 with reason code 'invalid-request', the field path and what was expected, so the caller can repair the request without reading the source.
The process stops and starts again.
Every hold and every sale is lost. The service answers again from the fixed inventory with every seat free. No reader can tell a lost sale from a seat that was never sold.
No module under src/domain contains an import whose specifier resolves into src/app or src/adapter, for every module under src/domain, including modules added after this change.
The repository holds no production code and no test, so there is no green oracle to observe before a move and no behaviour to preserve.

This change creates the first version of the HTTP JSON contract. The repository holds no other producer and no other consumer of it. The only consumer is the acceptance oracle in the same deployable, which changes in the same commit, so it is covered by the primary oracle. The possible later Svelte client is undecided and has no locator.

No party can change apart from the producer: there is no second deployable, no second release schedule and no persisted or wire datum that outlives the producer's version, because nothing survives a restart.

A seat may be held, confirmed, cancelled or left to expire, and the human fixed the deadline as authoritative with no grace window. How expiry is realized decides whether that promise can be kept, and the decision is hard to reverse once the store has a second writer.

Realize expiry lazily through one projection applied on every read and every command, keep one writer for the seat store, and verify the resulting state machine with Quint and Apalache, the progress promise with TLA+ and TLC, and the pure transition with Agda.

A background sweep that releases expired holds on a timer. Rejected: it adds a second writer whose run can lag the clock, and the Quint mutant that decides on the unprojected record shows a confirm taking effect after its deadline.

Release expired holds eagerly inside the clock advance operation. Rejected: it keeps the deadline promise only while the clock moves through that one operation, so the promise would be false for the system clock in normal use.
Accept a confirm shortly after the deadline through a grace window. Rejected: the human decided that there is no grace window.
Every read applies the projection, so a report is computed rather than stored. For one seating area this cost is not measurable; for a large inventory it would have to be measured.
Nothing happens at the moment a hold expires. No notification and no event can be emitted at the deadline without adding the timer this decision rejects.
The clock is a port, so the demonstration can move it. The same seam means the service trusts whoever holds the clock adapter.

Through the HTTP API a reader sees the whole fixed seating area: every seat of the configured inventory is listed exactly once and each is reported free, and the demo clock operation reports the time the service is using.

Start the service with the inventory ['s11','s12','s13'] and a hold duration of 120 seconds on an ephemeral port, then send GET /seats and then POST /demo/clock/advance with 30 seconds followed by a second GET /seats.

The first GET /seats answers 200 with a JSON body listing exactly the three configured seat identifiers, each with status 'free' and with no holder and no deadline. The advance answers 200 with the body {"now": <whole seconds>} and no other field, reporting a time thirty seconds later than the time reported before the call. The second GET /seats still lists the same three free seats, because moving the clock changes no seat that is free.

The oracle fails if the list is missing a configured seat, holds a seat that was never configured, reports any status other than 'free', leaks a hold reference field, answers prose instead of JSON, if the advance answer carries any field besides now, or if the advance operation does not move the reported time by exactly the seconds it was given.
The report of one seat, as the HTTP API answers it: the seat identifier and either free, or held with the holder name and the deadline, or sold with the owner name.

It never carries the hold reference, so it cannot tell two holds of the same booker with the same deadline apart, and it cannot tell a stored hold whose deadline has passed from a seat that was never held.
The report of the whole seating area: the report of every configured seat, in the configured order.
It cannot tell which hold reference is current, how many holds a seat has had, or how long a sold seat has been sold.

The outcome of one command, as the HTTP API answers it: the status code and either a granted hold with its reference and deadline, or a confirmation, or a cancellation, or a refusal with a machine reason code.
A refusal with reason no-such-hold cannot tell a wrong hold reference from one that never existed, which is deliberate so that no reference can be guessed from the answer.
The time the service is using, as the demo clock operation answers it, in whole seconds.
It cannot tell a system clock from a demonstration offset, and it carries no time zone and no date.

Two service states are equal when the inventory observation and the clock observation agree on them. This deliberately makes a stored hold whose deadline has passed equal to a free seat, which is the lazy expiry claim written as an equality.

A command walk over the fixed inventory: hold with a booker drawn from a closed set of three names, confirm or cancel with a hold reference drawn from the references already granted plus one reference that was never granted, and clock advances of whole seconds drawn from 1 to 300, all applied through the public service surface.

fast-check chooses the seed and prints it with the shrink path on failure. A failing seed and path are pinned into the same property as a replay case, so the counterexample runs again on every later run.
A confirm issued at exactly the deadline second of the hold it names.
A confirm issued exactly one second before the deadline of the hold it names.
A confirm and a cancel carrying a hold reference that was never granted for that seat.
A hold requested for a seat that is already held.
A clock advance larger than several hold durations in one call.
A hold and a confirm requested for a seat that is already sold.
Once the inventory observation reports a seat sold to a booker, every later inventory observation reports that seat sold to the same booker, whatever commands and clock advances follow.
The walk keeps its own record of the first booker each seat was ever sold to, built from the granted outcomes alone, and compares every later inventory observation with that record.
The law fails if any inventory observation reports a seat that was sold as free or held, or sold to a different booker.

A confirm or a cancel whose outcome observation is a success was sent strictly before the deadline the hold reported. At or after that deadline the outcome is a refusal with reason hold-expired and the seat report is free.
The walk reads the clock before each command and keeps the deadline the hold returned, then compares the two numbers itself without asking the service which branch it took.
The law fails if a success is observed while the clock observation is greater than or equal to the reported deadline, or if a command sent before the deadline is refused with hold-expired.
A confirm or a cancel carrying any value other than the hold reference the hold returned is refused, and the inventory observation after it equals the inventory observation before it.
The walk keeps the reference each hold returned and sends a different one, then compares the inventory observation taken before the command with the one taken after it.
The law fails if a command with a reference that was never granted for that seat changes any inventory observation or is answered as a success.
A hold is granted only when the seat report before the command is free. For any other seat report the outcome is a refusal and the inventory observation does not change.
The walk reads the seat report immediately before every hold and decides itself whether a grant was allowed.
The law fails if a hold is granted while the preceding seat report is held or sold, or if a refused hold changes the inventory observation.
After a command whose outcome observation is a refusal, the inventory observation and the clock observation are identical to the ones taken immediately before that command.
The walk takes the whole inventory observation and the clock observation before and after every command and compares the two snapshots field by field.
The law fails if any refusal changes a status, a holder, a deadline or the reported time, including a refused hold that quietly refreshes the deadline of the existing hold.
The deadline of a granted hold equals the clock observation taken at the moment of the grant plus the configured hold duration in seconds, for every seat and every booker.
The walk reads the clock observation immediately before the hold and adds the configured duration itself, instead of reading the number the service returned.
The law fails if any granted deadline differs from the independently computed sum, for example because the duration is read from a second place or a grace window is added.
Two inventory observations taken without any command and without any clock advance between them are equal.
The walk takes the inventory observation twice in a row at arbitrary points of the walk and compares the two results.
The law fails if reading the seating area changes it, for example because the report writes an expired hold back to the store.
For every granted hold, once the clock has been advanced past its deadline the seat report is free or sold, and never held.
The walk keeps every granted deadline and, after each clock advance, checks every seat whose deadline the new clock observation has passed.
The law fails if any seat is still reported held while the clock observation is greater than or equal to the deadline that hold reported.

Every response body parses against its declared response schema, and every refusal body carries a machine reason code from the closed set hold-expired, seat-held, seat-sold, no-such-hold, no-such-seat, invalid-request, together with a human message.
A granted hold answers 201 with a hold reference and a deadline.
A successful confirm answers 200 with the seat sold to the holder.
A successful cancel answers 200 with the seat free.
A confirm at or after the deadline answers 409 with reason code hold-expired.
A hold on a held seat answers 409 with reason code seat-held.
A hold or a confirm on a sold seat answers 409 with reason code seat-sold.
A confirm or a cancel with an unknown hold reference answers 404 with reason code no-such-hold.
A request for an unknown seat answers 404 with reason code no-such-seat.
The response shapes and the refusal reason codes are a closed finite set, so named cases cover the whole domain and generation would add no reachable case.

A future caller that reads the SeatStore port directly instead of going through the application service. The architectural check on dependency direction does not catch this one, so it stays an open risk carried by review.
A seat that is free and can be held by anybody.

Whether the demonstration clock operation must be refused outside the workshop. It is always available in this design and anybody who can reach the API can move the clock.
The human, as a deployment and exposure decision.
What a browser client needs in the wire format beyond the fields named here, which cannot be known until the Svelte question is decided.

What happens if the service is ever run as more than one process or on a runtime that interleaves handler bodies. The single-writer argument rests on one process and on handler bodies that run to completion.
The architect, as an explicit limit of the current design that must be reopened before any second process is added.
The state after a restart: every hold and every sale is lost and no reader can tell a lost sale from a seat that was never sold.
The human, who accepted in-memory state and no durable storage.
A ghost record of the first booker each seat was ever sold to. It exists only to state that a sale never changes, and has no counterpart in the service.
A ghost snapshot of the seat records before the current step, so that a refusal can be compared with the state it was supposed to leave alone.
A ghost snapshot of the sale record before the current step.
A ghost snapshot of the reference counter before the current step, so that a refusal that quietly consumes a reference is visible.

The Node.js runtime runs a request handler body to completion without interleaving another handler, so the read of the seat record, the decision and the write of the replacement happen in one uninterrupted turn of the event loop. There is one process and one store.
The initial state of the model: the configured inventory with every seat free and the clock at zero. In the service this is the composition root loading the inventory.
The service starts. The seating area is {stored} and the clock reads {clock}.
A booker asks to hold the seat at time {clock}. Before the request the seating area was {priorStored}; after it the seating area is {stored}. The service answered {last}.
A booker presents a hold reference to confirm the seat at time {clock}. Before the request the seating area was {priorStored}; after it the seating area is {stored}. The service answered {last}.
A booker presents a hold reference to cancel the hold at time {clock}. Before the request the seating area was {priorStored}; after it the seating area is {stored}. The service answered {last}.
The demonstration clock moves from {clock@pre} to {clock}. The stored seating area is {stored} and the service answered {last}.
A seat that has been sold stays sold to its first buyer for ever.
A seat reported as held always has a deadline that the clock has not yet reached.
Only a command carrying the hold reference of the current hold confirms or cancels it.

The predicate NoConfirmOneTickBeforeDeadline belongs to the model only. It is never a claim about the service: it is denied so that the checker produces the trace that illustrates it.
A witness that denies a confirm landing exactly one tick before the deadline, so that its counterexample is the trace where the confirm just succeeds.
The predicate NoConfirmExactlyAtDeadline belongs to the model only. It is never a claim about the service: it is denied so that the checker produces the trace that illustrates it.
A witness that denies a refusal with reason hold expired issued at exactly the deadline, so that its counterexample is the confirm-against-expiry race at the deadline second.
The predicate NoSoldSeatAfterTheDeadline belongs to the model only. It is never a claim about the service: it is denied so that the checker produces the trace that illustrates it.
A witness that denies a sold seat still being sold well after the old hold deadline, so that its counterexample shows that expiry never releases a sale.
The predicate NoSecondBookerRefused belongs to the model only. It is never a claim about the service: it is denied so that the checker produces the trace that illustrates it.
A witness that denies a refusal with reason seat held, so that its counterexample shows a second booker turned away.
A bound of the model. Two bookers, which is the smallest number that can compete for one seat.
A bound of the model. The clock ceiling of the model, set to six, which bounds an otherwise infinite state space.
A bound of the model. The hold references a command may present, including values that were never granted.
A bound of the model. The clock steps the demonstration operation may take, one or two time units.
Confirm and cancel read the stored seat record instead of the lazily expired projection, so a hold can be confirmed at or after its deadline.
A hold is granted on a seat that is already held for somebody else.
Cancel accepts any hold reference, so a booker who is not the holder cancels the hold.
The expiry projection is applied to sold seats as well, so a sold seat is reported free once the clock reaches twice the hold duration.
A refused hold still refreshes the deadline of the existing hold, so a refusal is not inert.
The deadline is never treated as reached, so a hold is reported as held for ever.
One seat, two bookers, a hold duration of two time units and a clock ceiling of six. Apalache explored every run of at most twelve steps within those bounds.
Each command is one atomic step. Two requests never interleave inside the model, which matches one Node.js process running handler bodies to completion and matches nothing else.
Model time is a whole number with no unit. The model says nothing about seconds, about latency or about the real clock.
The model carries no HTTP layer, no body parsing and no transport failure.

A countdown of abstract ticks that replaces absolute time, so that the state space is finite without a clock ceiling. The service keeps a deadline instead; the two agree on the order of events and on nothing else.
A booker holds the seat. The seating area becomes {status} held for {holder} with {remaining} ticks left.
The holder confirms. The seating area becomes {status} for {holder}.
The holder cancels. The seating area becomes {status} and the holder is {holder}.
The clock moves one tick. The hold has {remaining} ticks left and the seating area is {status}.
One tick is one abstract step of the clock. In the service the clock moves by itself and by the demonstration operation, and neither is atomic with a request.
A seat that is reported held eventually stops being reported held, whether by confirmation, by cancellation or by the deadline passing.
A sold seat is still observed as sold in every state of the projection.
A shape invariant of the model's own variables. It has no counterpart in the service, where the TypeScript checker carries the same duty.
Every seat has a status from the closed set, a holder from the closed set and a countdown within its bounds.
Two model values standing for any two distinct bookers. The service accepts any parsed booker name.
A model value standing for the absence of a holder. The service represents it by the free variant carrying no holder at all.

Weak fairness of the clock tick: while some hold still has time left, the clock eventually moves. In the service that obligation belongs to the operating system clock in normal use and to the demonstration operation during the workshop.
One seat, two bookers and a hold duration of two ticks. The whole state graph has nine distinct states, so the check is exhaustive within that projection.
A tick is an abstract step and never a second. The check establishes order of events, never elapsed time.
Deadlock checking is switched off, because a sold seat with no further command is a legitimate final state of this projection, where refusals are not modelled as steps.
Hold references and refusal reasons are projected away; the Quint model carries them.
A hold request on a seat that is already held renews that hold instead of being refused, so the clock keeps ticking while the seat is never released.
The pure transition takes a time, a command and a {SeatState}, and returns the next {SeatState} with its {Outcome}.
The transition is a pure function of its arguments. It performs no effect, so atomicity is a question for its single caller in the application service, not for the function.
The expiry projection takes a time and a {SeatState} and returns the {SeatState} every observation sees.
For every time, every command and every booker, applying the transition to a sold seat returns that same sold seat.
For every time, hold, reference and booker, if the outcome of a confirm on a held seat is a confirmation, then the time is strictly less than the deadline.
For every time, hold, reference and booker, if the outcome of a confirm on a held seat is a confirmation, then the reference presented equals the reference of the hold.
For every time, hold and reference, if the outcome of a cancel on a held seat is a cancellation, then the time is strictly less than the deadline.
For every time, hold and reference, if the outcome of a cancel on a held seat is a cancellation, then the reference presented equals the reference of the hold.
For every time, booker, reference, duration and seat state, if the outcome of a hold is a grant, then the projection of that seat state at that time is free.
For every time and every seat state, applying the expiry projection twice gives the same result as applying it once.
The module is accepted with the safe flag, so it holds no postulate, no hole and no unchecked termination. Totality of the transition is therefore checked, not asserted.
Bookers, references and times are natural numbers. The service uses strings and branded UUID values; the proof covers the ordering and equality those stand for, not their encoding.
The proof covers the pure transition alone. It says nothing about the store, the HTTP shell, concurrency or elapsed time.
The Agda definitions are a second writing of the same transition. Their agreement with the TypeScript implementation is an obligation the crafter carries, not a checked fact.
The transition reads the stored seat record instead of the expiry projection when confirming, so an expired hold can be confirmed. Agda refuses the module: the deadline property no longer holds.
The seating area is reported through the HTTP API: every configured seat appears exactly once with its current status, and the demonstration clock reports the time the service is using.
A booker holds a free seat through the HTTP API and the seat is then reported as held for that booker until a stated deadline.
The holder confirms their held seat through the HTTP API before its deadline and the seat is then reported as sold to that holder.
A second booker is refused a seat that is held or sold, and only the holder of the hold reference can confirm it, so one seat is never sold twice.
An unconfirmed hold is released, at once when the holder cancels and automatically when its deadline passes, and the seat is then reported free, while a sold seat is never released.

Weak fairness of the clock step: while some hold still has time left, the clock eventually moves. The operating system clock carries that obligation in normal use and the demonstration operation carries it during the workshop. Finite-state checking proves neither real scheduling nor elapsed seconds.
Apalache explored every run of at most twelve steps over one seat, two bookers, a hold duration of two time units and a clock ceiling of six. Outside those bounds the safety claim is not checked.
One process, one seat store, and request handler bodies that run to completion without interleaving.
No production code exists yet. Every runtime axis is designed and not built, and the acceptance oracles are the only thing that will move it.
Every observation of the seating area reports each configured seat exactly once and never reports a hold whose deadline has passed as held.
A configured inventory and a hold duration produce a service whose seating-area report can actually be built and answered.
The seat identifiers and hold duration the composition root reads when the process starts.
A reader reaches that report through GET /seats on the real HTTP port, with no private entry point.
An HTTP GET request for /seats on the port the service listens on.
Reporting the seating area is one synchronous request and one answer. It carries no progress obligation, so there is nothing for a temporal property to say about it.
A hold is granted only on a seat that is free at that moment, and the seat is then held for exactly one booker with exactly one deadline.
A free seat and a booker name produce a granted hold carrying a reference and a deadline.
A seat identifier from the configured inventory and a booker name parsed from the request body.
The booker reaches the grant through POST /seats/{seatId}/holds and sees the result through GET /seats/{seatId}.
An HTTP POST to /seats/{seatId}/holds carrying a booker name.
Granting a hold is one synchronous request and one answer. The promise that the hold is later released belongs to the fourth value, not to this one.
A confirmation takes effect only strictly before the deadline and only for the holder of the hold reference, and the resulting sale never changes.
A held seat and its own hold reference, presented before the deadline, produce a sale to the holder.
The hold reference returned by the hold that created the hold, and a clock value strictly below its deadline.
The holder reaches the sale through POST /seats/{seatId}/holds/{holdRef}/confirm and sees it through GET /seats/{seatId}.
An HTTP POST to /seats/{seatId}/holds/{holdRef}/confirm.
Confirming is one synchronous request and one answer, and a sale is final, so no progress obligation remains after it.
No seat is ever sold to two bookers: a hold is refused on a held or sold seat, a confirmation is refused for anyone but the holder, and every refusal leaves the seating area unchanged.
A held or sold seat and a second booker produce a refusal carrying a machine reason code.
A seat identifier whose current report is held or sold, and a booker name or hold reference that is not the holder's.
The second booker reaches the refusal through the same public hold and confirm routes any booker uses, and sees the unchanged seat through GET /seats/{seatId}.
An HTTP POST to the hold or confirm route for a seat that another booker already holds or owns.
A refusal is immediate and final. The human decided that there is no queue and no fairness promise about who gets a released seat, so no booker is owed eventual success.
An unconfirmed hold is released by cancellation or by the deadline passing, and a sold seat is never released by either.
A held seat whose deadline the clock has passed, or whose holder cancels, produces a free seat report that a new hold can use.
A held seat together with either its own hold reference for a cancellation or a clock value at or beyond its deadline.
The release is reached through POST /seats/{seatId}/holds/{holdRef}/cancel or through the demonstration clock operation, and is observed through GET /seats/{seatId}.
An HTTP POST to the cancel route, or an HTTP POST to /demo/clock/advance with enough seconds to pass the deadline.
Every hold eventually stops being reported as held, whether by confirmation, by cancellation or by the deadline passing.
One seat, two bookers and a hold duration of two ticks, over a state graph of nine states. A tick is an abstract step and never a second, so elapsed time remains an unchecked runtime obligation.
The confirm that just makes it: the booker confirms one tick before the deadline and the seat becomes sold.
The confirm against expiry at the deadline second: the booker holds the seat, the clock reaches the deadline, the booker confirms with the right reference and is refused because the hold expired.
The same race for a cancellation: the holder cancels at the deadline second and is refused because the hold has already expired.
The clock runs well past the old deadline and the sold seat is still sold, so expiry never releases a sale.
A second booker asks for a seat that is held and is refused, and the first booker keeps the seat.
What a service that reads the stored record instead of the expiry projection does: it accepts a confirmation after the deadline and sells a seat it had already reported free.
What a service that applies expiry to sold seats does: it reports a paid seat as free once enough time has passed.
What a service that grants a hold on a held seat does: it hands the same seat to a second booker while the first still holds it.

Agda refuses the mutant module docs/feature/last-seat/model/SeatSafetyMutant.agda, which drops the expiry projection from the confirm path, so the deadline property of the pure transition is falsifiable and not vacuous. The typed model grammar accepts a kill only from a state-model checker, so this rejection is carried by the module and its recorded run instead of a kill row.

package.json declares "type": "module" and engines.node matching the installed Node v24.9.0, and pins exact versions, with no range prefix, for typescript, vitest, fast-check, zod and @types/node. package-lock.json is committed so that the installation step is reproducible. Production source lives under src/ and tsconfig.json carries the strict settings the recorded user standards name, including strict, noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noImplicitReturns and noFallthroughCasesInSwitch. vitest.config.ts includes tests/**/*.test.ts and nothing else. No script beyond what the verification argv already calls is needed.
A hold whose body does not name the booker answers 400 with reason code invalid-request and the path of the field that failed.
A confirm or a cancel whose path carries a hold reference that is not a UUID answers 400 with reason code invalid-request and the path of the field that failed.
A demo clock advance whose body does not carry a positive whole number of seconds answers 400 with reason code invalid-request and the path of the field that failed.

The composition root in src/main.ts wires exactly one clock adapter, the advanceable clock of the Clock port, seeded from the system clock at start with a zero offset. No separate production clock adapter ships, because that clock with a zero offset already answers the system time and a second adapter nothing calls would be a name with no caller.

A cancel presented for a seat that is already sold is refused and changes nothing. The reason code of that refusal is undeclared: the oracle asserts the refusal and that the seat report and the seating area are unchanged, and asserts no reason code for it.

Each schema refusal of the wire is a case of its own: a hold that does not name the booker, a confirm or cancel path parameter that is not a UUID, and a demo clock advance that is not a positive whole number of seconds. Value 1 carries the missing booker case and the advance case, because the hold route and the demo clock route ship in value 1. Value 2 and value 4 carry the non-UUID hold reference case, because the confirm route ships in value 2 and the cancel route ships in value 4, and a path parameter of a route that does not yet exist cannot be refused for its shape.

The shared walking-skeleton obligation is discharged inside the value 1 oracle at tests/acceptance/hold-a-free-seat.test.ts, which carries it as an acceptance obligation of value 1: before any command GET /seats lists every configured seat exactly once, free, with no holder and no deadline, the demo clock operation answers {"now": <whole seconds>}, and an advance moves the reported time by exactly the seconds it was given. No separate shared oracle file ships.

The wire contract is: the service starts with 'node src/main.ts' and reads the seat inventory from SEAT_INVENTORY, the hold duration from HOLD_DURATION_SECONDS and the listening port from PORT, bound to 127.0.0.1. A seat report carries seatId, status, the holder of a held seat or the owner of a sold seat, and the deadline of a held seat. A successful confirm and a successful cancel answer 200 with the report of that seat. A refusal answers {reason, message}. The demo clock answers {now}. There is no read-only clock route. No seat report and no seating-area answer carries a hold reference.
